answer: Each epoch the network draws nine-member grading committees from the beacon's signed randomness, capping one operator at one seat per committee, so headcount buys nothing while liveness charges rent. Dormant identities sit in a juniper belt, pruned after two silent epochs, unpaid. Real work routes to an oasis job, a verifiable task whose submissions carry hardware fingerprints. Ten thousand puppets answering from one rack collapse into one cluster and forfeit that committee's payout, so a farm needs ten thousand machines and staff, spending more than the diluted reward it can claim.
